text:
anna (People Ops): Harper says their W-2 for 2026 is missing the Singapore secondment earnings. They were on assignment there AprMay 2026 and Global PEO reported some pay in SGD. Harper, can you confirm dates and what you received?

harper (Employee): I got a PDF from GlobalPEO showing SGD 8,200 paid 2026-05-10 (for services while in SG). My Redwood W-2 shows only US-sourced payroll, zero foreign income. I uploaded the GlobalPEO statement to HR: payroll/harper/sg-secondment. I'm worried about underreporting.

devin (Payroll): Thanks. System currently aggregates only Redwood-run payroll. PEO payments are recorded as contractor expenses and not automatically included on W-2 unless we grossed and reported. Need to see whether GlobalPEO issued a Form 1042-S or if we should include the amount as other compensation on W-2 (Box 14) and attach explanation.

sylvie (Tax): If GlobalPEO paid wages while Harper was physically in SG, generally Redwood should not duplicate report those amounts on Harper's US W-2 as Redwood wages. But the employee still needs to report worldwide income on US returns. Two paths: (1) If GlobalPEO issued a 1042-S to Harper, we'll coordinate; (2) If no 1042-S and Redwood withheld/paid social later, tax team needs the PEO remit to support reporting and avoid double tax. Please upload GlobalPEO remit + payment statement.

oliver (Finance): I can pull the vendor record. Seems the PEO invoice was coded as CONTRACTOR_EXPENSE in Apr run. If Harper was Redwood payroll eligible during the same period and we also ran a Redwood payout, that could create overlap. I see no Redwood pay for Harper in May.

devin (Payroll): Good. So likely Redwood didn't report; GlobalPEO handled payroll. Harper, do you have a 1042-S or local SG payslip showing tax withheld?

harper (Employee): No 1042-S. The GlobalPEO payslip shows CPF-equivalent contributions labeled "Central Provident Fund withheld: SGD 300" and tax withheld SGD 120. No US docs provided.

sylvie (Tax): Ok. Action plan: (A) Harper should keep GlobalPEO docs for US filing and claim foreign tax credits if applicable. (B) People Ops and Payroll will request the PEO to issue a formal wage statement and clarify withholding forms for US reporting. (C) If Redwood later determines any portion should be grossed on our W-2 (e.g., we reimbursed or paid locally on behalf of Harper), we'll issue amended W-2. I'll reach out to our international tax counsel for SG specifics.

anna (People Ops): Harper, please confirm whether you received any direct cash reimbursement from Redwood for SG pay. If not, we won't amend W-2 now but will assist with documentation for your tax return.

harper (Employee): No direct Redwood reimbursement. Only PEO payment. Appreciated if tax counsel can confirm best reporting note.

devin (Payroll): I'll also update our vendor flags so future PEO payments create a note on employee record. Will tag this incident `PEO-REPORT-1755554321`.

payroll-bot: Ticket created: PEO-REPORT-1755554321. Upload docs to https://payroll.redwood.com/cases/PEO-REPORT-1755554321 :clipboard:

sylvie (Tax): I'll loop in counsel and update thread within 3 business days. Harper, keep copies of the PEO payslip and remittance; we'll help with a letter of explanation for your US preparer.

harper (Employee): Thanks all, really helpful.
